## How it works

- [statement] Make repeated triggers harmless: Chainlink says completed work must change state so the same subset is no longer eligible, and AWS recommends caller-provided request identifiers for recognizing duplicate requests. Inference for an LP bot: give each intended action a durable identity and reconcile its outcome before issuing another action for the same intent; an offchain identifier alone does not enforce onchain idempotency. (medium confidence) — https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-automation/reference/automation-interfaces · keywords: Automated LP bot architecture and operational safety · also: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/
- [statement] Persist operation identity and request parameters together when implementing an idempotent control API: AWS describes atomic recording of the token and mutations, and rejecting reused identifiers when parameters change. This is evidence for durable intent records, not a claim that a local database commit can atomically commit a blockchain transaction. (low confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/ · keywords: Automated LP bot architecture and operational safety

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A timeout is an ambiguous outcome, not evidence of absence of side effects. AWS recommends connection and request timeouts, capped backoff, a limit on retry attempts, a single retry layer where practical, and jitter; apply these controls to bot RPC dependencies and reconcile state-changing operations before retrying them. (low confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/ · keywords: Automated LP bot architecture and operational safety
- [statement] Gamma attributed its January 2024 vault exploit to an arithmetic error in automation scripts that configured deposit safety settings, and reported that halting deposits stopped the attack vector while withdrawals remained possible; the operational lesson inferred here is to validate applied risk configuration and rehearse selective emergency controls. (low confidence) — https://gammastrategies.medium.com/post-mortem-remediation-plan-9a62f10d90f3 · keywords: Automated LP bot architecture and operational safety

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Architecture recommendation inferred from the documented check/perform pattern: separate observation and planning from state-changing execution; the execution boundary must recheck current conditions rather than trust an earlier plan. Chainlink documents offchain checks and onchain performance as one example of this separation, without establishing present service availability. (low confidence) — https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-automation/reference/automation-interfaces · keywords: Automated LP bot architecture and operational safety
- [statement] Base derivation distinguishes unsafe, safe, and finalized chain state and can reorganize above the safe block. Architectural inference: store block identity with observations, treat provisional observations as revisable, and replay/reconcile affected bot records after a reorganization instead of declaring every observed inclusion permanent. (low confidence) — https://docs.base.org/base-chain/specs/protocol/consensus/derivation · keywords: Automated LP bot architecture and operational safety
- [statement] Google recommends monitoring latency, traffic, errors, and saturation and keeping paging noise low. Inference for an LP bot: instrument dependency latency and errors, job throughput and backlog, and alert on actionable loss of progress rather than paging on every transient retry. (low confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/ · keywords: Automated LP bot architecture and operational safety

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Bound each automated work item: Chainlink recommends limiting check and execution ranges and splitting work across registrations to keep execution inside predictable gas limits. For an LP controller, bounding the number of positions handled per job is an application of that pattern. (low confidence) — https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-automation/reference/automation-interfaces · keywords: Automated LP bot architecture and operational safety
- [statement] OpenZeppelin documents an authorized emergency stop, but inheriting the pause module does not automatically protect every function: the relevant function modifiers must actually be applied. A bot-owned executor needs explicit coverage of the critical entry points it intends to stop. (low confidence) — https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts/5.x/api/utils · keywords: Automated LP bot architecture and operational safety
- [statement] Do not assume a dependency circuit breaker is automatically the best retry control: AWS warns that circuit breakers introduce modal behavior that is difficult to test and can delay recovery, and describes local token-bucket retry limits as an alternative. This caution concerns dependency overload handling, not a reason to omit an emergency stop for bot-controlled financial operations. (low confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/ · keywords: Automated LP bot architecture and operational safety
